paper_title: A low boiling-point and low-cost fluorinated additive improves the efficiency and stability of organic solar cells

knowledge_points.content: 1,4-Difluorobenzene (DFB) is identified as a promising solvent additive for organic solar cells due to its low boiling point of 88.8 °C (361.95 K) and low cost (approximately 4.05 RMB/g).
knowledge_points.evidence: Herein, we propose a low boiling-point and low-cost additive 1,4-difluorobenzene (DFB) with a boiling point of 88.8 °C... Moreover, DFB is a cheap chemical product (the price of DFB with a purity of 99% (J&K) is 4.05 RMB/1 g).

knowledge_points.content: The power conversion efficiency (PCE) of organic solar cells based on the J71:m-ITTC blend increased from 11.01% to 12.38% upon the addition of 0.8% v/v 1,4-difluorobenzene (DFB).
knowledge_points.evidence: The power conversion efficiency (PCE) of the OSCs based on J71:m-ITTC with the DFB additive treatment increased to 12.38% from 11.01% for the device without the additive treatment.

knowledge_points.content: Optimized J71:m-ITTC devices treated with DFB additive exhibit a short-circuit current density (Jsc) of 19.27 mA/cm², an open-circuit voltage (Voc) of 0.874 V, and a fill factor (FF) of 73.54%.
knowledge_points.evidence: Table 1: 0.8% DFB: Voc 0.874, Jsc 19.27 mA cm-2, FF 73.54%, PCEmax 12.38%.

knowledge_points.content: The DFB additive treatment enhances intermolecular pi-pi stacking and molecular aggregation in J71:m-ITTC blends, which facilitates more efficient charge carrier separation and transport.
knowledge_points.evidence: The DFB additive treatment enhances intermolecular π-π stacking of the photovoltaic materials, which is conducive to charge carrier separation and transport... The results suggest that the DFB additive treatment could promote the aggregation of J71 and m-ITTC.

knowledge_points.content: Bimolecular recombination is suppressed in J71:m-ITTC devices when treated with 0.8% DFB, as evidenced by the increase in the power-law exponent (alpha) from 0.915 to 0.969.
knowledge_points.evidence: For the J71:m-ITTC-based device, the α value is 0.915 without additive treatment, and 0.969 for the device with the 0.8% DFB additive treatment. This result indicates that bimolecular recombination was suppressed.

knowledge_points.content: DFB additive treatment improves charge carrier mobility in J71:m-ITTC films, increasing hole mobility (μh) from 7.3 x 10^-4 to 8.83 x 10^-4 cm² V^-1 s^-1 and electron mobility (μe) from 1.50 x 10^-5 to 4.37 x 10^-5 cm² V^-1 s^-1.
knowledge_points.evidence: The hole (μh) and electron (μe) mobilities of the J71:m-ITTC blend film is 7.3 × 10−4 cm2 V−1 s−1 and 1.50 × 10−5 cm2 V−1 s−1, respectively. With 0.8% DFB additive treatment, the hole and electron mobilities were boosted to 8.83 × 10−4 cm2 V−1 s−1 and 4.37 × 10−5 cm2 V−1 s−1.

knowledge_points.content: The optimized fabrication process for the J71:m-ITTC active layer involves a donor:acceptor weight ratio of 1:1.2, a total concentration of 18 mg/mL in chloroform, and 0.8% v/v DFB additive followed by thermal annealing at 150 °C for 2 minutes.
knowledge_points.evidence: The optimized weight ratio of J71:m-ITTC is 1:1.2... with a total blend concentration of 18 mg mL−1 in chloroform, and the optimized additive treatment condition is 0.8% v/v... followed by thermal annealing at 150 °C for 2 min.

knowledge_points.content: GIWAXS analysis reveals that the DFB additive combined with thermal annealing results in tighter molecular packing in the blend, with the (010) pi-pi diffraction peak shifting to 1.724 Å^-1 (d-spacing of 3.645 Å).
knowledge_points.evidence: The thermally annealed J71:m-ITTC blend film with additive treatment had a (100) diffraction peak of 0.305 Å−1 (d spacing: 20.630 Å) and a (010) π-π diffraction peak of 1.724 Å−1 (d-spacing: 3.645 Å).

knowledge_points.content: Devices treated with DFB show superior long-term storage stability, retaining 87.23% of their initial PCE after 200 hours in a nitrogen-filled glovebox, compared to a larger decline in untreated devices.
knowledge_points.evidence: After 200 h storage of the OSC devices with the additive and TA treatment in a N2-filled glove box, the PCE slightly declined from 12.22% to 10.66%, keeping 87.23% of the original energy conversion efficiency.

knowledge_points.content: The morphological stability under thermal stress (150 °C) is improved with DFB treatment, retaining 84% of initial PCE after 30 minutes compared to 81% for devices without the additive.
knowledge_points.evidence: After 30 min [at 150 °C], the PCE is 9.01% and 10.34%, respectively, which are 81% and 84% of their initial values. Therefore, the morphological stability of the additive-treated film was also slightly improved.

knowledge_points.content: Low boiling point additives like DFB are preferred for roll-to-roll printing on flexible substrates because they can be removed at temperatures that do not cause deformation of plastic substrates.
knowledge_points.evidence: In addition, low boiling point additives are necessary in roll-to-roll printing for fabricating flexible OSCs because high temperature annealing will inevitably cause deformation of the plastic substrate of the flexible devices.

knowledge_points.content: AFM measurements show that the RMS roughness of the J71:m-ITTC blend film increases slightly from 0.683 nm to 0.750 nm after treatment with 0.8% DFB and thermal annealing.
knowledge_points.evidence: For the J71:m-ITTC blend without DFB additives... RMS roughness of only 0.683 nm. After adding 0.8% DFB and thermal annealing (TA), the roughness of the blended film increased slightly to 0.750 nm.
